stem: Which pair has the same relationship as KEYBOARD : KEY?
hints: Look at the order. Which comes first here: the whole or the part?
Make a bridge sentence that keeps the order: "A keyboard is made up of many keys."
Test each pair in the same order: "A ___ is made up of many ___." A pair with the part first does not match, even if the two things are related.

solution.methodName: Make a bridge sentence, then test each choice

steps.action: Make a bridge sentence in the same order as the stem: "A keyboard is made up of many keys."
steps.why: The whole (keyboard) comes first and the part (key) comes second. The answer must follow the same order.

steps.action: Test stairs : step. "Stairs are made up of many steps" is true. The whole comes first and the part second.
Test leaf : tree. "A leaf is made up of many trees" is false. Here the part comes first, so the order is reversed.
Test glove : hand. A glove covers a hand. A glove is not made up of hands.
Test computer : desk. A computer sits on a desk. It is not made up of desks.

trapNotes.leaf : tree: A leaf is part of a tree, but here the part comes first. The stem puts the whole first (keyboard, then key), so this pair is in reversed order.
trapNotes.glove : hand: A glove is worn over a hand. It covers the hand, but it is not made up of hands.
trapNotes.computer : desk: A computer is placed on a desk. This is a thing and its place, not a whole and its parts.
